Comment 11 • 3 days ago


Hi :emilio, :lars. Adding some extra info here after I hit the same issue as bug 2037923 on Windows Nightly, but during normal use instead of shutdown. AFAIU this bug's patch would help with that. The main thread hung while showing a tooltip. The hang lasted about 5 to 10 minutes and then resolved on its own. I took a full dump with Task Manager during the hang and can share it privately on request. Below are the results of analyzing the hang dump with an LLM companion.

Build 20261030090406. The process had been running for 4:30 when the dump was taken. It was the first start after updating from 20261029212358, so the startup cache was being rebuilt from scratch. At the time, other processes were most likely using the disk heavily: I had a test harness running that downloads and extracts Firefox builds and runs throwaway installs.

Main thread, blocked on mTableLock:

mozilla::detail::MutexImpl::lock
mozilla::scache::StartupCache::GetBuffer
ReadCachedStencil
mozJSModuleLoader::LoadSingleModule
mozilla::loader::SyncModuleLoader::StartFetch
mozJSModuleLoader::ImportESModule
mozilla::xpcom::ConstructESModuleComponent
nsGetServiceByContractID::operator()          (nsITooltipTextProvider)
mozilla::dom::XULTooltipElement::PostHandleEvent
nsXULPopupManager::ShowTooltipAtScreen
nsXULTooltipListener::sTooltipCallback        (timer)


Holder, BgIOThreadPool #7, inside the regular (timer-driven) write:

ntdll!NtWriteFile
KERNELBASE!WriteFile
nss3!PR_Write
mozilla::scache::Write
mozilla::scache::StartupCache::WriteToDisk
StartupCache::MaybeWriteOffMainThread::<lambda>
nsThreadPool::Run


What this adds:

The hang is not limited to shutdown. Bug 2026686 made the write use nsAutoLowPriorityIO, and bug 2037923 only reverted that for the shutdown write. The regular write still runs with THREAD_MODE_BACKGROUND_BEGIN while holding mTableLock for the whole WriteToDisk, so any main-thread module load that hits the startup cache blocks until the write finishes. Here the module load was triggered lazily by a tooltip.
The writer was not doing any work. !runaway shows about 0.12 s of total CPU on that thread, and no other Firefox thread was doing file I/O. It was simply stuck in NtWriteFile at background I/O priority while other processes used the disk.
WriteToDisk issues several small PR_Write calls per entry (a frame header, then the compressed body), with a seek between entries and no batching in user space. With the 428 entries being written here, that is around 860 non-empty write requests that Windows can delay at background priority, which stretches the time the lock is held.
The first session after an update is the worst case: the whole cache is rewritten soon after startup, while the user is actively using the browser.
Hangs like this one do not reach crash-stats. In the parent process, a main-thread hang only produces a crash report when it happens during shutdown, where the shutdown terminator crashes the process with a shutdownhang signature. Outside shutdown, nothing kills the process: the hang either resolves, as here, or the user kills Firefox, and neither case files a report. The shutdownhang signature from bug 2037923 therefore only covers the shutdown case. Background hang reports (BHR) do record main-thread hangs and are the place to measure how often this happens, though only on Nightly.
The bug 2037923 fix doesn't stop a regular write that is already running at low priority when shutdown starts. Consistent with that, shutdownhang | mozilla::scache::StartupCache::GetBuffer still appears on releases 155 to 159 in the last 30 days, at low volume. It also shows up on ESR 140 and on releases before 152, which never had the low-priority change, so some of these crashes likely have a different cause.

Possible mitigations until the locking split from this bug relands:

Have GetBuffer use a try-lock, as PutBuffer already does, and treat a busy lock as a cache miss so the module is compiled from source instead of blocking.
Drop aUseLowPriorityIO for the initial and regular writes as well, as bug 2037923 did for shutdown. Low priority only makes sense once mTableLock is no longer held during the I/O.
